messages:
helen: FYI a community contributor reported flaky failures when running the "ambassador" Next + LangChain starter on Cloudflare Workers. Behavior: some SSR calls to /api/respond return 401 or TypeError: AbortController is not a constructor. Locally (node) it's fine.

omar: Interesting. Are they using the JS SDK in the worker? Cloudflare workers have a different global env (no AbortController constructor historically).

helen: Yes, they wired the SDK directly in the edge handler. Snippet from their route: ```js
import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'
const client = createClient({ apiKey: RW_KEY })
export default async function onRequest(context) {
  const body = await context.request.json()
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(await client.generate({ prompt: body.q })))
}
```
They deployed to Cloudflare and saw sporadic TypeError + a small % of 401s.

yun: Two separate things: (1) abort/timeout plumbing in Workers (fetch + AbortSignal) and (2) token refresh singleflight + fetch polyfills. The SDK uses AbortController for timeouts and a node-oriented refresh lock. In workers the AbortController shape can be different or missing.

omar: Could be a dependency that assumes globalThis.AbortController exists. Clouds can be inconsistent. If the SDK polyfills AbortController at runtime, that may interfere with transpilation and cause the TypeError.

yun: For the 401s: if the SDK triggers a token refresh, it does an internal fetch to the auth endpoint. Workers by default may block egress to internal auth endpoints in some tenant setups, causing refresh to fail and inflight callers to surface 401 without retries.

helen: Proposal for the starter: add a short "Cloudflare / Workers notes" section in README and a small shim in the template that checks for globalThis.AbortController and polyfills a tiny one if missing, plus an opt-in RW_WORKER_RETRY to enable a 1-retry fallback for 401s. Also add a comment recommending setting up a refresh-proxy if you use hosted short-lived keys.

omar: That sounds reasonable. For the SDK, we should: (A) ensure it uses a web-safe singleflight Promise so workers behave correctly, (B) avoid relying on nonstandard AbortController internals, and (C) surface clear errors when refresh egress fails instead of silent falls-through.

yun: I'll open an SDK issue titled "js-sdk: worker-safe refresh + timeout" with a small repro that runs in the Cloudflare Workers emulator, fires 80 concurrent requests, and simulates a blocked refresh endpoint. Expected: single refresh attempt, inflight callers wait, then retry automatically.

helen: For the starter repo changes I'll add: - README Cloudflare notes - optional tiny AbortController polyfill file (imports only when polyfill flag set) - opt-in RW_WORKER_RETRY=true wrapper for server routes - one integration test in CI that runs on a Workers emulator and asserts <0.5% 401s on a 500-request spike

omar: Also double-check serialization of embeddings between the Node sample and the Python eval harness. We had a previous bug where the JS side sent arrays of strings for compactness ("0.123"), and Python's eval expected floats, causing a ValueError in numpy parsing.

yun: Good catch. Add a small normalization helper in the sample: ensure embeddings are Number typed and sent as list-of-lists for consistency. For the eval harness, add a tolerant parser that casts strings to floats. I'll add that to the SDK eval utils too.

helen: I'll open the starter PR with the opt-in workarounds and link the SDK issue. We'll keep the polyfill behind a feature flag so we don't hide real errors for users who should use long-lived keys or a proxy.

release-bot: Preview deploy created for helen/ambassador-worker-fixes (workers-emulator) - build 2026.04.02-781

omar: Thanks. Once yun lands the SDK patch we should revert the worker retry and polyfill in the sample and add a short migration note in the README.

yun: ETA for SDK patch: 3 business days (unit + worker-emulator tests included). I'll also add a changelog entry and the reproducer to the issue.

helen: Awesome. PR description will call out the exact tradeoffs and show the tiny helper code we'll use in the sample. Ping me if you want to review the README wording. :raised_hands:
